title: Determining the effects of loss of function mutations in human cell lines
protocol: Place the cell vial in a water bath set at 37°C for 2-5 min to thaw fibroblasts and lymphoblastoid cells.
Transfer the contents of the vial to a 15 mL conical tube containing 5 mL of warm (∼37°C) complete culturing medium.
Centrifuge the tube at 500 g for 5 min to obtain a pellet of cells.
Aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the cell pellet.
Add 10 mL of warm (∼37°C) complete medium and gently resuspend the pellet by pipetting up and down.
Transfer 10 mL of complete medium containing the cells to a T25 flask or 10 cm cell culture-treated dish.
Replace the medium with fresh complete medium the next day.
Aspirate the medium from the cells.
Add 10 mL of warm (∼37°C) fresh complete medium.
Replace the medium the next day with fresh medium.
Aspirate the medium from the plate without disturbing the cells.
Add 5 mL of PBS to rinse the remaining medium from the plate.
Add 1 mL of warm Trypsin-EDTA to the center of the plate.
Place the plate in the incubator for 5 minutes.
Mechanically detach the cells using a P1000 pipette.
Add 4 mL of fibroblast culturing medium.
Transfer the volume in a 1:4 or 1:5 ratio to a new 10 cm dish.
Pipette up and down five times using a 10 mL serological pipette.
Transfer the cells into a new 50 mL conical tube.
Take 10 μL of the cell suspension for counting.
Seed 200,000–300,000 cells/mL in a new T25 flask.
Seed human patient or control fibroblast cell lines in 6-well plates.
Harvest cells at 80% confluency (1 × 10^6 cells) for fibroblasts, and collect lymphoblastoid cells at 6 × 10^6 confluence.
Clean the work surface and pipettes with RNase decontamination solutions such as RNaseZap.
Use only filtered pipette tips during RNA extraction.
Work in a clean environment to prevent RNA degradation.
Handle QIAzol Lysis Reagent with caution under a chemical fume hood.
Extract total RNA using the miRNeasy Mini kit (Qiagen).
Add 700 μL QIAzol Lysis Reagent to the cell pellet in a 1.7 mL tube.
Lysate cells by pipetting vigorously around 20 times up and down using a p200 pipette set at 200 μL.
Incubate the lysed sample at room temperature for 5 min.
Add 140 μL of chloroform to the QIAzol lysate mix.
Shake the mixture vigorously for 15 seconds.
Incubate the mixed sample at room temperature for 3 minutes.
Centrifuge the lysate for 15 minutes, 12,000 g at 4°C.
Transfer the upper aqueous phase carefully to a new collection tube.
Add 1.5 volumes of 100% ethanol to the aqueous phase.
Load up to 700 μL of sample into a RNeasy Mini column placed in a 2 mL collection tube.
Centrifuge at 11,000 rpm for 15 seconds at room temperature, discarding the flow-through.
Add 350 μL buffer RWT to the RNAeasy Mini column and spin for 15 seconds at 11,000 rpm.
Discard the flow-through from the column.
Mix 10 μL DNAseI stock solution with 70 μL buffer RDD gently by inverting the tube.
Add 80 μL of DNAseI reaction directly on the RNAeasy Mini column filter.
Incubate for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Add 350 μL buffer RWT to the RNeasy spin column and centrifuge for 15 seconds at 11,000 rpm.
Add 700 μL of RWT buffer to wash the column.
Centrifuge at 11,000 rpm for 30 s and discard the flow-through.
Add 500 μL of RPE wash buffer into the RNAeasy Mini column.
Centrifuge at 11,000 rpm for 30 s and discard the flow-through.
Add 500 μL of RPE wash buffer into the RNAeasy Mini column.
Centrifuge at 11,000 rpm for 2 min.
Place the RNeasy Mini column into a new 1.5 mL collection tube and centrifuge at full speed for 1 min.
Transfer the RNeasy Mini column to a new 1.5 mL collection tube.
Add pre-warmed (60°C) 30–50 μL RNase-free water directly into the column membrane.
Incubate for 5 minutes, then centrifuge at 11,000 rpm for 1 min.
Quantify RNA using NanoDrop 1000.
Prepare a 3× bromophenol blue loading dye by diluting the commercial 6× loading dye 1:1 in formamide.
Rinse the gel chamber and the comb once with NaOH 0.4N.
Rinse the gel chamber and the comb four to five times with abundant deionized water.
Let the gel chamber and comb dry before use.
Mix 3 μL of 3× formamide bromophenol blue loading dye with 1 μg of extracted RNA.
Bring the mix volume up to 9 μL with nuclease-free water to obtain a 1× loading dye solution.
Mix gently without vortexing.
Spin down quickly.
Incubate at 60°C for 10 min.
Place on ice for 2 min.
Load 9 μL of RNA/dye solution onto the 1% agarose TAE gel.
Run the gel at low speed until the loading blue runs over half of the gel.
Thaw gDNA wipeout buffer, Quantiscript Reverse Transcriptase, Quantiscript RT Buffer, RT Primer Mix, and RNase-free water on ice.
Mix each thawed solution by flicking the tubes.
Centrifuge briefly to collect residual liquid from the sides of the tubes.
Store the mixed solutions on ice.
Thaw previously frozen RNA on ice.
Prepare the genomic DNA elimination reaction on ice, adding 2 μL of gDNA wipeout buffer to a tube containing 1 μg of RNA.
Bring the volume up to 12 μL with nuclease-free water.
Incubate for 8 min at 42°C.
Place the mixture immediately on ice after incubation.
Do not incubate at 42°C for longer than 10 minutes.
Add 1 μL of RT Primer Mix to each reaction tube.
Add 4 μL of Quantiscript RT Buffer to each reaction tube.
Add 1 μL of Quantiscript Reverse Transcriptase to each reaction tube.
Incubate the tubes at 42°C for 30 minutes.
Incubate the tubes at 95°C for 3 minutes to inactivate Quantiscript Reverse Transcriptase.
Store the cDNA at 4°C for short-term storage or at -20°C for long-term storage.
Aspirate the medium from the plate without disturbing the cells.
Add 5 mL of phosphate buffer (PBS) 1× to rinse the plate from the remaining medium.
Add 1 mL of warm (∼37°C) Trypsin-EDTA 1×.
Place the plate in the incubator for 5 min.
Mechanically detach the cells by pipetting up and down with a P-1000 pipette.
Add 4 mL of fibroblast culturing medium.
Transfer the cells into a 15 mL conical tube and centrifuge at 500 g for 5 min.
Aspirate the medium without disturbing the pellet.
Add 300 μL of cold RIPA buffer completed with phosphatase and protease inhibitors 1×.
Dissolve the pellet by pipetting up and down for 10–15 times using a P-1000 pipette.
Transfer the 300 μL of lysate into a 1.7 mL Eppendorf tube.
Place the tube in ice for 20 min.
Centrifuge for 20 min at 21,000 g at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a new 1.7 mL Eppendorf tube and place it on ice.
Quantify the protein concentration using the Pierce BCA Protein Assay Kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific).
Prepare a bovine serum albumin (BSA) standard curve with concentrations of 2 μg/μL, 1 μg/μL, and 0.5 μg/μL.
Mix reagent A and B in a ratio of 50:1 for a total volume of 40 μL per sample.
Add 38 μL of the BCA mix to a new Eppendorf tube.
Add 2 μL of protein extract to each tube.
Vortex and spin the tubes briefly.
Incubate the tubes at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Analyze the absorbance at 562 nm using the NanoDrop OneC (Thermo Scientific).
Based on the standard curve, calculate the protein concentration in mg/mL.
Mix the extracted protein with NuPAGE Reducing Agent 10× and NuPAGE LDS Sample Buffer 4×.
Consider a final volume of 30 μL–40 μL per well if using the 1.5 mm 10-wells gel or 20 μL–30 μL per well if using the 1.5 mm 15-wells gel.
Denature the proteins at 95°C for 10 minutes.
Pour 100–150 mL of running buffer to cover the bottom of the mini cell chamber.
Place a NuPAGE 4%–14% Bis-Tris Gel (10 wells, 1.5 mm) in a mini gel cassette.
Clean the wells of the gel by pipetting up and down 100-150 μL of running buffer into them.
Load the samples onto the gel.
Run the gel at 70 V until the dye front surpasses the stacking gel, then increase to 120 V.
Prepare 1 L of transfer solution for protein transfer.
Activate the nitrocellulose membrane in methanol or transfer solution for 20-30 s.
Pour 500 mL of transfer buffer into the wide-set glass container and another 500 mL into the transfer apparatus.
Place the sandwich with the black side facing down.
Immerse a sponge into the transfer buffer for 10 seconds and place it over the black side of the sandwich.
Open the gel support and carefully detach the acrylamide gel from the plastic support using filter paper.
Place the filter paper and the acrylamide gel over the sponge with the gel facing up.
Gently put the nitrocellulose membrane over the acrylamide gel.
Immerse a filter paper in the transfer buffer for 5 seconds and place it over the nitrocellulose membrane.
Immerse the roller into the transfer buffer and gently roll over the chromatography paper to remove air bubbles.
Immerse a sponge into the running buffer for 10 seconds and place it on top of the chromatography paper.
Close the sandwich and place it into the apparatus with the black side facing down.
Transfer 500 mL from the wide-set glass container to the transfer apparatus.
Run the transfer applying a constant current of 340 mA for 90 min in cold room (4°C).
Prepare blocking solution by dissolving 2.5 g of nonfat milk in 50 mL of TBS-T 1× to obtain a 5% milk solution.
Remove the nitrocellulose membrane with transferred proteins from the transfer apparatus.
Incubate the membrane with the blocking solution (5% milk in TBS-T 1×) for at least 30 min at room temperature.
Rinse the membrane once or twice with TBS-T 1× to remove excess milk.
Incubate the membrane with the antibody of interest dissolved in TBS-T 1× containing 3% BSA and 0.02% Sodium Azide, following the manufacturer’s data sheet concentration, overnight at 4°C.
Wash membranes with TBS-T 1× for 10 min each for three times.
Incubate the membrane with secondary antibody HRP-conjugated dissolved in milk (5%) at a final dilution of 1:10,000 for at least 1 h at room temperature.
Use ECL solution to reveal images on the blot.
Acquire blots on the G:BOX Chemi XX9 machine using GeneSys software 1.6.5.0.
Determine gel exposures by the software.
Optimize dilution rates for primary and secondary antibodies according to antibody specifications, protein of interest, cell lines, and tissue.
Run western blots starting from highest recommended antibody dilution ratios until clear bands are visualized in the gel.
Test primary antibody dilutions in both TBS-T 1×-BSA 3% and TBS-T 1× with 5% non-fat milk to determine which provides better resolution.
Avoid running gels faster than 120 V for proteins weighing more than 90 kDa to minimize smearing.
Ensure maximum protein transfer from the gel to the membrane to achieve correct quantification.
Incubate HEK293T cells at 37°C in a humidified chamber supplemented with 5% CO2.
Seed HEK293T cells in 12 well-plates at a density of 0.1 × 10^6 cells/well.
Dilute the desired amount of DNA in 75 μL of jetPRIME buffer, vortex for 10 s and quickly spin down.
Add 1.6 μL of jetPRIME reagent.
Vortex briefly.
Spin down and incubate for 10 min at room temperature.
Add the transfection mix to each well.
Place the plate in the incubator for 48 h.
Aspirate the medium containing the transfection mix the day after transfection.
Replace with fresh complete culture medium.
Collect the cells after 48 h post-transfection.
Process the collected cells for RNA or protein extraction.
Design primers for mutagenesis using QuikChange software.
Prepare the sample reaction mix according to the protocol.
Run the PCR as specified in the protocol table.
Add 1 μL of DpnI restriction enzyme (10 U/μL) directly to each reaction tube once the PCR is completed.
Gently but thoroughly mix each reaction mixture by pipetting the solution up and down several times.
Spin down the reaction mixtures in a microcentrifuge for 1 min.
Incubate the reactions at 37°C for 1 h to digest the parental supercoiled dsDNA.
Gently thaw XL10-Gold ultracompetent cells on ice.
Aliquot 45 μL of the ultracompetent cells to a prechilled 14-mL BD Falcon polypropylene round-bottom tube.
Add 2 μL of β-ME mix and gently swirl contents.
Incubate cells on ice for 10 min, swirling every 2 min.
Transfer 2 μL of Dpn I-treated DNA from each reaction to separate aliquots of ultracompetent cells.
Swirl transformation reactions gently to mix.
Incubate reactions on ice for 30 min.
Heat-pulse tubes in a 42°C water bath for 30 s.
Incubate tubes on ice for 2 min.
Add 0.5 mL of preheated (42°C) NZY+ broth to each tube.
Incubate tubes at 37°C for 1 h with shaking at 225-250 rpm.
Plate appropriate volume of each transformation reaction on agar plates containing the appropriate antibiotic.
Incubate transformation plates at 37°C for >16 hours.
